verdict.reasoning: Patient says, "I've been having this, blinding headache for a few days... I find it very hard to focus or, like I can't even go to work" and later clarifies it started three days ago.
Onset: "I woke up one morning with a headache, and that was three days ago" (sudden upon waking). Constancy: "Kinda all the time... then I still have it, it's still there."
Location: "it's kind of all over but, I feel like over my right eye, it's um bit, stronger" supports holocephalic with greater intensity over the right eye.

Photophobia: "lights definitely make me more sensitive... I don't really, like strong lights." Visual phenomena: "I get this, shooting light sometimes... weird kind of vision." Nausea without emesis: "Uh, no, feeling a bit sick, but no vomiting."
Severity: "I guess it's mostly, eight, and then it kinda comes down to maybe a five" and ibuprofen gives partial relief: "when I take Ibuprofen it gets a bit better... but then I still have it."
Sleep: "Um, yeah, I'm, sleeping well" and "Is it waking you up in the night-time?" / "No, no, no. But I can wake up with it in the morning."
Positional/head movement worsening: "Sometimes when I stand up, quickly I get a bit of a, stabbing pain. Um, or if I throw my head like, it I kind of feel like something is moving inside."

Negatives: "no" to tingling, numbness, weakness; "No, none at all" to change in smell or taste; no fever noted and patient says "I don't really feel, feverish or anything"; and "No, no" to cold symptoms, sore throat, sore ears, pain over sinuses, cough or phlegm; "No" to nosebleeds.

Past headaches: "I recently had a, a one for like two days, um, but it just went away with Ibuprofen" and "it's just um, a bit of a pressure, in between my eyes... But nothing major" and later "No nothing, none of those" to flashing lights, nausea, vomiting with past headaches.
Recent eye exam: "Um, yeah, actually had one recently and, nothing changed my vision."

When asked about other medical problems: "Um, I think I only had a, a pain, um, when I was younger but, no causes found and that went away, but that's, the only thing I know of." This supports essentially no ongoing past medical history.
Medications: "Um, just the pill" and started "about a year ago"; also "apart from the Ibuprofen that I take, sometimes when, the headache gets really bad, nothing else."
Allergies: "And any allergies to anything?" / "No."
Family history: "my mum, suffers from, like she has migraines... she's like, has the vomiting and everything."
Living situation: "Who do you live with at home?" / "Uh, just by myself." Work: "Um, I work from home..."
Work impact: "couldn't really manage to, do it all the time. So sometimes I just took a day off" and description of missing part/all of multiple days due to inability to focus from headache.
Smoking: "And do you smoke?" / "Uh, no." Alcohol: "Do you drink any alcohol regularly?" / "Yeah"; "probably like, three , once a week" (≈3 units once weekly).
Travel: "Have you been abroad recently at all?" / "No."

Acute severe 3‑day headache with photophobia and visual phenomena is described. Doctor states: "it could possibly be a migraine type headache" and later references "these flashing lights"; no focal neuro symptoms and no infectious symptoms are elicited (no fever, neck stiffness, URI signs).

Doctor says: "we'll check your blood pressure as well... because sometimes if we, if we do think it's a migraine, then you would have to change your pill. If you've had these flashing lights, and things like that" and explains that in that case "we'd have to change it to something else."
Work impairment: patient reports difficulty focusing and not being able to go to work and details taking time off and stopping work early because of the headache.

Plan: "we probably should, book you into an appointment to get an examination... we should do a neurological examination, look at the back of your eyes as well" and later "we'll check your blood pressure as well."

Medication plan: "I can prescribe you something, similar to Ibuprofen, but a bit stronger... And you can also take Paracetamol at the same time" and "start, the medication which I prescribe to you, take it with food."

OCP plan: "But you can carry on with that for the moment" and earlier: "because sometimes if we, if we do think it's a migraine, then you would have to change your pill... It wouldn't be suitable to stay on that pill, particularly, we'd have to change it to something else."

Safety‑netting: "if in the meantime before your appointment your, headache is getting unbearable, getting worse or changing. Then , um, if it's that bad, then you should go to A and E and have an examination. Um, , you can call us for further advice on that."
Follow‑up: "obviously , if it settles, in the meantime then, we can cancel that" referring to the booked examination appointment.
